title: Bill 111 on removing belongings from public places
summary: On November 21, 2024, the chair urged commissioners to watch a December 3 meeting and review Bill 111, which covers removal and storage of personal property. A testifier said people could not get back belongings taken in homeless sweeps. The council had sent the bill to committee in July.

timeline.text: The committee deferred the bill with no objections.
timeline.body: County Council Water Authority, Social Services, and Parks Committee

timeline.text: The vice chair said he wants the administration's feedback on the amended bill before it is posted.
timeline.body: County Council Water Authority, Social Services, and Parks Committee

timeline.text: The chair said the meeting was needed to meet a 90-day timeline.
timeline.body: County Council Water Authority, Social Services, and Parks Committee

timeline.text: The chair said the vice chair will likely bring amendments to the bill after the budget.
timeline.body: County Council Water Authority, Social Services, and Parks Committee

timeline.text: The county lawyer agreed to send members a written summary of the court case.
timeline.body: County Council Water Authority, Social Services, and Parks Committee

timeline.text: The vice chair said the bill would use the term "safe space" instead.
timeline.body: County Council Water Authority, Social Services, and Parks Committee

timeline.text: The pro tem asked that the bill not use the Hawaiian word puʻuhonua.
timeline.body: County Council Water Authority, Social Services, and Parks Committee

timeline.text: The vice chair said 45 days of notice matches what people in houses get before an eviction.
timeline.body: County Council Water Authority, Social Services, and Parks Committee

timeline.text: Closing oral testimony: Members agreed with no objections to close oral testimony.
timeline.body: County Council Water Authority, Social Services, and Parks Committee

timeline.text: She said Bill 111 requires storing property for 90 days, while most other ordinances she found use about 30 days.
timeline.body: County Council Water Authority, Social Services, and Parks Committee

timeline.text: She said the court does not require the 45 days of notice in Bill 111.
timeline.body: County Council Water Authority, Social Services, and Parks Committee

timeline.text: The chair said the meeting kept the bill in committee to allow more talks.
timeline.body: County Council Water Authority, Social Services, and Parks Committee

timeline.text: The chair said the bill sets steps to relocate people compassionately when needed, with access to services and storage of their property.
timeline.body: County Council Water Authority, Social Services, and Parks Committee

timeline.text: The committee held a special meeting on Bill 111 (2024), about removing and storing personal property in public places.
timeline.body: County Council Water Authority, Social Services, and Parks Committee

timeline.text: The chair urged commissioners to watch a December 3 meeting and review the bill.
timeline.body: Commission on Healing Solutions for Homelessness

timeline.text: A testifier said people could not get back belongings taken in homeless sweeps.
timeline.body: Commission on Healing Solutions for Homelessness

timeline.text: The committee deferred the bill with no objections.
timeline.body: County Council Water Authority, Social Services, and Parks Committee

timeline.text: The administration and outreach providers agreed to work together on the bill before the committee meets again.
timeline.body: County Council Water Authority, Social Services, and Parks Committee

timeline.text: Remove storage and recovery fee section: Members agreed by consensus to drop the section allowing a fee for storing and recovering property.
timeline.body: County Council Water Authority, Social Services, and Parks Committee

timeline.text: Notice photos available upon request: Members agreed by consensus that notice photos be made available on request instead of posted on a County website.
timeline.body: County Council Water Authority, Social Services, and Parks Committee

timeline.text: Informational meeting before encampment removal: Members agreed by consensus to require an informational meeting at the site at least four days before a removal.
timeline.body: County Council Water Authority, Social Services, and Parks Committee

timeline.text: The committee chose to revisit a proposal to cut the notice before a camp removal from 45 days to 14.
timeline.body: County Council Water Authority, Social Services, and Parks Committee

timeline.text: A resource person asked for an immediate moratorium, or pause, on sweeps (clearing of homeless camps).
timeline.body: County Council Water Authority, Social Services, and Parks Committee

timeline.text: The committee will invite a County director to help define Hawaiian words used in the bill.
timeline.body: County Council Water Authority, Social Services, and Parks Committee

timeline.text: Remove the word puʻuhonua from the bill: Members agreed by consensus not to use the word puʻuhonua in the bill.
timeline.body: County Council Water Authority, Social Services, and Parks Committee

timeline.text: The committee decided not to vote on changes today and to note only where members agreed.
timeline.body: County Council Water Authority, Social Services, and Parks Committee

timeline.text: The chair said the bill will come back at the next meeting with more chances for testimony.
timeline.body: County Council Water Authority, Social Services, and Parks Committee

timeline.text: A testifier strongly supported the bill's section on finding other shelter before a camp is removed.
timeline.body: County Council Water Authority, Social Services, and Parks Committee

timeline.text: The committee is working on Bill 111, which sets steps for relocating people and storing their personal property.
timeline.body: County Council Water Authority, Social Services, and Parks Committee

timeline.text: The committee discussed Bill 111, which sets rules for removing and storing property in public places and creates a right to shelter.
timeline.body: County Council Water Authority, Social Services, and Parks Committee

timeline.text: Referral of Bill 111 (removal and storage of personal property): The council sent Bill 111 to committee.
timeline.body: County Council Meeting
